Definition: feminine of a presumed derivative of G4253 as noun; the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel:--forepart(-ship).
BiblicalUsage: Prora is the prow, the forward part of the ship, and Luke uses it twice in the storm. The sailors let down a boat under colour of casting anchors out of the foreship, and when the ship runs aground the forepart sticks fast while the hinder part is broken. The spelling in the Greek text carries the old diphthong, but the word is the same prow.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the prow that stuck fast is the picture of a voyage God meant to end on that shore, and no sailor's trick could change it.
